objects.definition: typedef void (*GLFWglproc)(void);
objects.description: Function pointer type for client API (OpenGL / OpenGL ES) procedure addresses returned by glfwGetProcAddress. Pointer-to-function type; you do not instantiate it directly beyond storing function addresses.

objects.definition: typedef void (*GLFWvkproc)(void);
objects.description: Function pointer type for Vulkan procedure addresses returned by glfwGetInstanceProcAddress or loader. Pointer-to-function type; store Vulkan function addresses.

objects.definition: typedef struct GLFWmonitor GLFWmonitor;
objects.description: Opaque handle type representing a monitor. Incomplete type in this header; implementation-private. Lifetime is managed by GLFW; users obtain via glfwGetMonitors/glfwGetPrimaryMonitor and never free directly.

objects.definition: typedef struct GLFWwindow GLFWwindow;
objects.description: Opaque handle type representing a window and its associated context/surface. Incomplete type here. Create with glfwCreateWindow and destroy with glfwDestroyWindow.

objects.definition: typedef struct GLFWcursor GLFWcursor;
objects.description: Opaque handle type representing a mouse cursor object. Create with glfwCreateCursor or glfwCreateStandardCursor; destroy with glfwDestroyCursor. Set on a window via glfwSetCursor.

objects.definition: typedef void* (* GLFWallocatefun)(size_t size, void* user);
objects.description: Callback function pointer type for custom allocation. Used in GLFWallocator. Must return a suitably aligned block or NULL. Not to call GLFW from within.

objects.definition: typedef void* (* GLFWreallocatefun)(void* block, size_t size, void* user);
objects.description: Callback function pointer type for custom reallocation used by GLFWallocator. Must handle non-NULL block and size > 0. Return aligned block or NULL.

objects.definition: typedef void (* GLFWdeallocatefun)(void* block, void* user);
objects.description: Callback function pointer type for custom deallocation used by GLFWallocator. Will be passed non-NULL block. Must not call GLFW.

objects.definition: typedef void (* GLFWerrorfun)(int error_code, const char* description);
objects.description: Callback function pointer type for GLFW error handling. Set via glfwSetErrorCallback; GLFW invokes on errors.

objects.definition: typedef void (* GLFWwindowposfun)(GLFWwindow* window, int xpos, int ypos);
objects.description: Callback type for window position changes. Register via glfwSetWindowPosCallback.

objects.definition: typedef void (* GLFWwindowsizefun)(GLFWwindow* window, int width, int height);
objects.description: Callback type for window size changes. Register via glfwSetWindowSizeCallback.

objects.definition: typedef void (* GLFWwindowclosefun)(GLFWwindow* window);
objects.description: Callback type for window close request. Register via glfwSetWindowCloseCallback.

objects.definition: typedef void (* GLFWwindowrefreshfun)(GLFWwindow* window);
objects.description: Callback type for window content refresh. Register via glfwSetWindowRefreshCallback.

objects.definition: typedef void (* GLFWwindowfocusfun)(GLFWwindow* window, int focused);
objects.description: Callback type for window focus changes. Register via glfwSetWindowFocusCallback.

objects.definition: typedef void (* GLFWwindowiconifyfun)(GLFWwindow* window, int iconified);
objects.description: Callback type for window iconify/restore events. Register via glfwSetWindowIconifyCallback.

objects.definition: typedef void (* GLFWwindowmaximizefun)(GLFWwindow* window, int maximized);
objects.description: Callback type for window maximize/restore events. Register via glfwSetWindowMaximizeCallback.

objects.definition: typedef void (* GLFWframebuffersizefun)(GLFWwindow* window, int width, int height);
objects.description: Callback type for framebuffer size changes. Register via glfwSetFramebufferSizeCallback.

objects.definition: typedef void (* GLFWwindowcontentscalefun)(GLFWwindow* window, float xscale, float yscale);
objects.description: Callback type for window content scale changes. Register via glfwSetWindowContentScaleCallback.

objects.definition: typedef void (* GLFWmousebuttonfun)(GLFWwindow* window, int button, int action, int mods);
objects.description: Callback type for mouse button events. Register via glfwSetMouseButtonCallback.

objects.definition: typedef void (* GLFWcursorposfun)(GLFWwindow* window, double xpos, double ypos);
objects.description: Callback type for cursor position events. Register via glfwSetCursorPosCallback.

objects.definition: typedef void (* GLFWcursorenterfun)(GLFWwindow* window, int entered);
objects.description: Callback type for cursor enter/leave events. Register via glfwSetCursorEnterCallback.

objects.definition: typedef void (* GLFWscrollfun)(GLFWwindow* window, double xoffset, double yoffset);
objects.description: Callback type for scroll events. Register via glfwSetScrollCallback.

objects.definition: typedef void (* GLFWkeyfun)(GLFWwindow* window, int key, int scancode, int action, int mods);
objects.description: Callback type for key events. Register via glfwSetKeyCallback.

objects.definition: typedef void (* GLFWcharfun)(GLFWwindow* window, unsigned int codepoint);
objects.description: Callback type for Unicode character input. Register via glfwSetCharCallback.

objects.definition: typedef void (* GLFWcharmodsfun)(GLFWwindow* window, unsigned int codepoint, int mods);
objects.description: Deprecated callback type for Unicode character input with modifiers. Register via glfwSetCharModsCallback. Scheduled for removal in 4.0.

objects.definition: typedef void (* GLFWdropfun)(GLFWwindow* window, int path_count, const char* paths[]);
objects.description: Callback type for file/path drop events. Register via glfwSetDropCallback.

objects.definition: typedef void (* GLFWmonitorfun)(GLFWmonitor* monitor, int event);
objects.description: Callback type for monitor connect/disconnect events. Register via glfwSetMonitorCallback.

objects.definition: typedef void (* GLFWjoystickfun)(int jid, int event);
objects.description: Callback type for joystick connection events. Register via glfwSetJoystickCallback.
POD struct describing a video mode (resolution, color bit depths, refresh rate). Returned by glfwGetVideoMode(s). Arrays are managed by GLFW; do not free.
POD struct describing a monitor gamma ramp with per-channel lookup tables. Ownership of arrays is by GLFW when returned; when passing to glfwSetGammaRamp, arrays are copied.
POD struct for 2D image data (RGBA8 pixel buffer) used for window icons and custom cursors. Caller owns memory when providing to GLFW; GLFW copies on use.
POD struct containing standardized gamepad button and axis states used by glfwGetGamepadState.
POD struct bundling custom allocation callbacks and a user pointer. Set via glfwInitAllocator before glfwInit. All function pointers must be non-NULL.

functions.name: glfwInit
functions.description: Initializes the GLFW library so other GLFW functions can be used. Call once before using most GLFW APIs. Returns GLFW_TRUE on success, GLFW_FALSE on failure.
requirements: Must be called from the main thread
Should be called before most other GLFW functions
On failure, GLFW is terminated internally; you may call again
If successful, you should call glfwTerminate before application exit

functions.name: glfwTerminate
functions.description: Terminates GLFW, destroying remaining windows/cursors, restoring gamma ramps, and freeing resources. After calling, GLFW must be re-initialized with glfwInit to use most APIs again.
requirements: Must be called from the main thread
Must not be called from within a GLFW callback (non-reentrant)
Any remaining window contexts must not be current on other threads when called

functions.name: glfwInitHint
functions.signature: GLFWAPI void glfwInitHint(int hint, int value);
functions.description: Sets an initialization hint controlling the next glfwInit. Has effect only during the next initialization; values persist until changed or termination.
requirements: Must be called from the main thread
May be called before glfwInit
hint must be a valid init hint token; value must be valid for that hint

functions.name: glfwInitAllocator
functions.description: Sets a custom heap memory allocator to be used by GLFW during the next initialization. Pass NULL to use default allocator.
requirements: Must be called from the main thread
Every function pointer in the provided GLFWallocator must be non-NULL (else emits GLFW_INVALID_VALUE)
Allocator functions must not call GLFW functions
Allocator must support being called during glfwInit (before initialized) and during glfwTerminate (after uninitialized)
Returned memory must be suitably aligned for any object type
Allocator is copied before the function returns

functions.name: glfwInitVulkanLoader
functions.description: Sets the Vulkan vkGetInstanceProcAddr function GLFW will use for Vulkan entry point queries during initialization. Useful on platforms where the loader cannot be found dynamically.
requirements: Must be called from the main thread
May be called before glfwInit
loader may be NULL to request GLFW to dynamically load the standard Vulkan loader

functions.name: glfwGetVersion
functions.signature: GLFWAPI void glfwGetVersion(int* major, int* minor, int* rev);
functions.description: Retrieves the GLFW library version numbers of the running binary. Any of the output pointers may be NULL.
requirements: May be called before glfwInit
Output pointers, if non-NULL, must be valid for writing

functions.name: glfwGetVersionString
functions.description: Returns a static ASCII string describing the GLFW library build (version, platforms, compiler and options). Not for parsing version/platform support.
requirements: May be called before glfwInit
Returned pointer is static and valid for the lifetime of the library; do not free

functions.name: glfwGetError
functions.description: Returns and clears the last error code for the calling thread, optionally returning a UTF-8 description pointer.
requirements: May be called before glfwInit
If description is non-NULL, it will be set to a pointer owned by GLFW; valid until the next error or GLFW termination; do not free

functions.name: glfwSetErrorCallback
functions.description: Sets the global error callback that GLFW calls whenever an error occurs. Returns the previously set callback.
requirements: Must be called from the main thread
May be called before glfwInit
callback may be NULL to clear
Error description string is valid only until callback returns; copy if needed

functions.name: glfwGetPlatform
functions.description: Returns the platform selected during initialization (e.g., GLFW_PLATFORM_WIN32, _COCOA, _WAYLAND, _X11, _NULL).
requirements: GLFW must be initialized
May be called from any thread

functions.name: glfwPlatformSupported
functions.description: Returns whether the library binary includes support for the specified platform token.
requirements: platform must be one of the documented GLFW_PLATFORM_* tokens
May be called before glfwInit
May be called from any thread

functions.name: glfwGetMonitors
functions.description: Returns an array of handles to all currently connected monitors; primary is first. Returns NULL if none or on error.
requirements: Must be called from the main thread
count must be a valid pointer for writing (set to zero on error)
Returned array is owned by GLFW; valid until monitor configuration changes or GLFW terminates; do not free

functions.name: glfwGetPrimaryMonitor
functions.description: Returns the primary monitor handle, or NULL if no monitors were found or on error.
requirements: Must be called from the main thread

functions.name: glfwGetMonitorPos
functions.signature: GLFWAPI void glfwGetMonitorPos(GLFWmonitor* monitor, int* xpos, int* ypos);
functions.description: Returns the position of the upper-left corner of the monitor in screen coordinates.
requirements: Must be called from the main thread
monitor must be a valid monitor handle
Output pointers may be NULL; if error, non-NULL outputs are set to zero

functions.name: glfwGetMonitorWorkarea
functions.signature: GLFWAPI void glfwGetMonitorWorkarea(GLFWmonitor* monitor, int* xpos, int* ypos, int* width, int* height);
functions.description: Returns position and size of the monitor work area (not obscured by task bars).
requirements: Must be called from the main thread
monitor must be a valid monitor handle
Any output pointer may be NULL; on error, non-NULL outputs are set to zero

functions.name: glfwGetMonitorPhysicalSize
functions.signature: GLFWAPI void glfwGetMonitorPhysicalSize(GLFWmonitor* monitor, int* widthMM, int* heightMM);
functions.description: Returns the physical size of the monitor display area in millimetres.
requirements: Must be called from the main thread
monitor must be valid
Output pointers may be NULL; on error, non-NULL outputs set to zero

functions.name: glfwGetMonitorContentScale
functions.signature: GLFWAPI void glfwGetMonitorContentScale(GLFWmonitor* monitor, float* xscale, float* yscale);
functions.description: Retrieves the content scale (DPI scale relative to platform default) for the monitor.
requirements: Must be called from the main thread
monitor must be valid
Output pointers may be NULL

functions.name: glfwGetMonitorName
functions.description: Returns a UTF-8 human-readable name of the monitor (make/model).
requirements: Must be called from the main thread
monitor must be valid
Returned string is owned by GLFW; valid until monitor disconnect or GLFW termination; do not free

functions.name: glfwSetMonitorUserPointer
functions.signature: GLFWAPI void glfwSetMonitorUserPointer(GLFWmonitor* monitor, void* pointer);
functions.description: Associates a user-defined pointer with a monitor object.
requirements: monitor must be valid
May be called from any thread (unsynchronized)
May be called from monitor callback, including during disconnect

functions.name: glfwGetMonitorUserPointer
functions.description: Returns the user pointer previously set on the monitor, or NULL if none.
requirements: monitor must be valid
May be called from any thread (unsynchronized)
May be called from monitor callback, including during disconnect

functions.name: glfwSetMonitorCallback
functions.description: Sets the monitor configuration callback (connect/disconnect). Returns previously set callback.
requirements: Must be called from the main thread
GLFW must be initialized
callback may be NULL to clear

functions.name: glfwGetVideoModes
functions.signature: GLFWAPI const GLFWvidmode* glfwGetVideoModes(GLFWmonitor* monitor, int* count);
functions.description: Returns a sorted array of all video modes supported by the monitor.
requirements: Must be called from the main thread
monitor must be valid
count must be a valid pointer for writing (set to zero on error)
Returned array is owned by GLFW; valid until monitor disconnect, a subsequent call for the same monitor, or GLFW termination

functions.name: glfwGetVideoMode
functions.description: Returns the current video mode of the monitor.
requirements: Must be called from the main thread
monitor must be valid
Returned pointer is owned by GLFW; valid until monitor disconnect or GLFW termination

functions.name: glfwSetGamma
functions.signature: GLFWAPI void glfwSetGamma(GLFWmonitor* monitor, float gamma);
functions.description: Generates a gamma ramp from the given positive finite exponent and sets it for the monitor.
requirements: Must be called from the main thread
monitor must be valid
gamma must be a finite number greater than zero
Wayland: feature unavailable (emits GLFW_FEATURE_UNAVAILABLE)

functions.name: glfwGetGammaRamp
functions.description: Returns the current gamma ramp for the monitor.
requirements: Must be called from the main thread
monitor must be valid
Returned structure and arrays are owned by GLFW; valid until monitor disconnect, subsequent call for same monitor, or GLFW termination
Wayland: feature unavailable (returns NULL and emits error)

functions.name: glfwSetGammaRamp
functions.signature: GLFWAPI void glfwSetGammaRamp(GLFWmonitor* monitor, const GLFWgammaramp* ramp);
functions.description: Sets the gamma ramp for the monitor. The original ramp is restored on glfwTerminate.
requirements: Must be called from the main thread
monitor must be valid
ramp must point to a gamma ramp whose size should match the current ramp size (Win32 size must be 256)
Wayland: feature unavailable
The ramp is copied before return

functions.name: glfwDefaultWindowHints
functions.description: Resets all window hints to their default values for the next glfwCreateWindow.
requirements: Must be called from the main thread
GLFW must be initialized

functions.name: glfwWindowHint
functions.signature: GLFWAPI void glfwWindowHint(int hint, int value);
functions.description: Sets an integer window hint for the next glfwCreateWindow. Values persist until changed or reset.
requirements: Must be called from the main thread
GLFW must be initialized
hint must be a valid window hint token; value must be appropriate

functions.name: glfwWindowHintString
functions.signature: GLFWAPI void glfwWindowHintString(int hint, const char* value);
functions.description: Sets a string window hint for the next glfwCreateWindow.
requirements: Must be called from the main thread
GLFW must be initialized
hint must be a string-type window hint
value string is copied by GLFW before return

functions.name: glfwCreateWindow
functions.signature: GLFWAPI GLFWwindow* glfwCreateWindow(int width, int height, const char* title, GLFWmonitor* monitor, GLFWwindow* share);
functions.description: Creates a window and associated OpenGL/OpenGL ES context (unless client API hint is GLFW_NO_API). For fullscreen, pass a monitor; otherwise windowed. Context may share resources with 'share'.
requirements: Must be called from the main thread
GLFW must be initialized
width and height must be greater than zero
If creating OpenGL ≥ 3.2 on macOS, set GLFW_OPENGL_PROFILE accordingly (3.0/3.1 not supported on macOS)
If share is non-NULL, its context must not be current on any other thread on Win32
If client API hint is GLFW_NO_API, no context is created
To use Vulkan surface, window must be created with client API = GLFW_NO_API

functions.name: glfwDestroyWindow
functions.description: Destroys the specified window and its context. No more callbacks will be called for that window.
requirements: Must be called from the main thread
GLFW must be initialized
Must not be called from a GLFW callback (non-reentrant)
The context for this window must not be current on any other thread

functions.name: glfwWindowShouldClose
functions.description: Returns the value of the window close flag.
requirements: May be called from any thread (unsynchronized)
window must be a valid window handle

functions.name: glfwSetWindowShouldClose
functions.signature: GLFWAPI void glfwSetWindowShouldClose(GLFWwindow* window, int value);
functions.description: Sets the window close flag value (to override or signal close).
requirements: May be called from any thread (unsynchronized)
window must be valid

functions.name: glfwGetWindowTitle
functions.description: Returns the current UTF-8 window title as set by creation or glfwSetWindowTitle.
requirements: Must be called from the main thread
window must be valid
Returned string is owned by GLFW; valid until next title get/set or termination; do not free

functions.name: glfwSetWindowTitle
functions.signature: GLFWAPI void glfwSetWindowTitle(GLFWwindow* window, const char* title);
functions.description: Sets the UTF-8 title of the window.
requirements: Must be called from the main thread
window must be valid
title must be a valid UTF-8 string

functions.name: glfwSetWindowIcon
functions.signature: GLFWAPI void glfwSetWindowIcon(GLFWwindow* window, int count, const GLFWimage* images);
functions.description: Sets the icon for the window from one or more candidate images, or resets to default with count=0.
requirements: Must be called from the main thread
window must be valid
count >= 0; if count > 0, images must point to count valid GLFWimage entries whose pixel data pointers are valid; data is copied
Pixels must be 32-bit little-endian non-premultiplied RGBA, arranged top-left to bottom-right
macOS/Wayland: feature unavailable (emits GLFW_FEATURE_UNAVAILABLE)

functions.name: glfwGetWindowPos
functions.signature: GLFWAPI void glfwGetWindowPos(GLFWwindow* window, int* xpos, int* ypos);
functions.description: Returns the position of the upper-left corner of the window content area.
requirements: Must be called from the main thread
window must be valid
Any output pointer may be NULL; on error non-NULL outputs set to zero
Wayland: feature unavailable

functions.name: glfwSetWindowPos
functions.signature: GLFWAPI void glfwSetWindowPos(GLFWwindow* window, int xpos, int ypos);
functions.description: Sets the position of the upper-left corner of the content area of a windowed-mode window.
requirements: Must be called from the main thread
window must be valid and in windowed mode
Wayland: feature unavailable
Do not use to move already visible windows unless necessary (user experience)

functions.name: glfwGetWindowSize
functions.signature: GLFWAPI void glfwGetWindowSize(GLFWwindow* window, int* width, int* height);
functions.description: Retrieves the size of the content area of the window in screen coordinates.
requirements: Must be called from the main thread
window must be valid
Output pointers may be NULL; on error non-NULL outputs set to zero

functions.name: glfwSetWindowSizeLimits
functions.signature: GLFWAPI void glfwSetWindowSizeLimits(GLFWwindow* window, int minwidth, int minheight, int maxwidth, int maxheight);
functions.description: Sets size limits for the content area of the window. Applied immediately to windowed windows and may resize them.
requirements: Must be called from the main thread
window must be valid
All dimensions must be >= 0 or GLFW_DONT_CARE
Maximums must be >= minimums if specified
Wayland: limits take effect on next resize
If limits conflict with aspect ratio limits, results are undefined

functions.name: glfwSetWindowAspectRatio
functions.signature: GLFWAPI void glfwSetWindowAspectRatio(GLFWwindow* window, int numer, int denom);
functions.description: Sets required aspect ratio for window content area. Applied immediately to windowed windows and may resize them.
requirements: Must be called from the main thread
window must be valid
numer and denom must be > 0 or GLFW_DONT_CARE
Wayland: applied on next resize
If conflicts with size limits, results are undefined

functions.name: glfwSetWindowSize
functions.signature: GLFWAPI void glfwSetWindowSize(GLFWwindow* window, int width, int height);
functions.description: Sets the size of the window content area. For fullscreen windows, updates desired video mode resolution.
requirements: Must be called from the main thread
window must be valid
width and height are in screen coordinates

functions.name: glfwGetFramebufferSize
functions.signature: GLFWAPI void glfwGetFramebufferSize(GLFWwindow* window, int* width, int* height);
functions.description: Retrieves the size of the window framebuffer in pixels.
requirements: Must be called from the main thread
window must be valid
Output pointers may be NULL; on error non-NULL outputs set to zero

functions.name: glfwGetWindowFrameSize
functions.signature: GLFWAPI void glfwGetWindowFrameSize(GLFWwindow* window, int* left, int* top, int* right, int* bottom);
functions.description: Retrieves the size of each edge of the window frame in screen coordinates (always zero or positive).
requirements: Must be called from the main thread
window must be valid
Any output pointer may be NULL; on error non-NULL outputs set to zero

functions.name: glfwGetWindowContentScale
functions.signature: GLFWAPI void glfwGetWindowContentScale(GLFWwindow* window, float* xscale, float* yscale);
functions.description: Retrieves the content scale (DPI scale) for the window, which may depend on which monitor it is on.
requirements: Must be called from the main thread
window must be valid
Output pointers may be NULL

functions.name: glfwGetWindowOpacity
functions.description: Returns the opacity (0.0–1.0) of the whole window including decorations. Returns 1.0 if unsupported.
requirements: Must be called from the main thread
window must be valid

functions.name: glfwSetWindowOpacity
functions.signature: GLFWAPI void glfwSetWindowOpacity(GLFWwindow* window, float opacity);
functions.description: Sets the opacity (0.0–1.0) of the whole window including decorations.
requirements: Must be called from the main thread
window must be valid
opacity must be a positive finite number between 0 and 1
Wayland: feature unavailable
Windows with framebuffer transparency should not also use whole-window transparency (undefined results)

functions.name: glfwIconifyWindow
functions.description: Iconifies (minimizes) the window if not already iconified. Restores the original video mode for fullscreen.
requirements: Must be called from the main thread
window must be valid

functions.name: glfwRestoreWindow
functions.description: Restores the window if iconified or maximized. For iconified fullscreen, sets desired video mode again.
requirements: Must be called from the main thread
window must be valid
Wayland: only restores from maximization

functions.name: glfwMaximizeWindow
functions.description: Maximizes the window if not already maximized. Does nothing for fullscreen windows.
requirements: Must be called from the main thread
window must be valid

functions.name: glfwShowWindow
functions.description: Makes the window visible if previously hidden. May focus it depending on hints/attributes.
requirements: Must be called from the main thread
window must be valid
Wayland: becomes visible after next framebuffer update, not immediately

functions.name: glfwHideWindow
functions.description: Hides the window if previously visible.
requirements: Must be called from the main thread
window must be valid

functions.name: glfwFocusWindow
functions.description: Brings the window to the front and sets input focus.
requirements: Must be called from the main thread
window must be valid
Use sparingly; focus stealing is disruptive
Wayland: compositor may ignore focus requests unless another window of same app has focus

functions.name: glfwRequestWindowAttention
functions.description: Requests user attention for the window (or application if per-window unsupported).
requirements: Must be called from the main thread
window must be valid
macOS: requests attention for the application, not a specific window

functions.name: glfwGetWindowMonitor
functions.description: Returns the monitor the window is using for fullscreen mode, or NULL if windowed.
requirements: Must be called from the main thread
window must be valid

functions.name: glfwSetWindowMonitor
functions.signature: GLFWAPI void glfwSetWindowMonitor(GLFWwindow* window, GLFWmonitor* monitor, int xpos, int ypos, int width, int height, int refreshRate);
functions.description: Switches a window between fullscreen (on monitor) and windowed mode and sets size/placement/video mode parameters.
requirements: Must be called from the main thread
window must be valid
If monitor is NULL (windowed), uses position and size; refreshRate ignored
Wayland: window position arguments are ignored
OpenGL/ES context remains valid; update viewport if framebuffer size changes

functions.name: glfwGetWindowAttrib
functions.signature: GLFWAPI int glfwGetWindowAttrib(GLFWwindow* window, int attrib);
functions.description: Returns the value of a window or context attribute.
requirements: Must be called from the main thread
window must be valid
attrib must be a valid window attribute token
Zero may be a valid attribute value; do not treat zero as error indication

functions.name: glfwSetWindowAttrib
functions.signature: GLFWAPI void glfwSetWindowAttrib(GLFWwindow* window, int attrib, int value);
functions.description: Sets certain window attributes (DECORATED, RESIZABLE, FLOATING, AUTO_ICONIFY, FOCUS_ON_SHOW, MOUSE_PASSTHROUGH).
requirements: Must be called from the main thread
window must be valid
attrib must be one of the supported set; value is GLFW_TRUE or GLFW_FALSE
Wayland: GLFW_FLOATING not supported (emits GLFW_FEATURE_UNAVAILABLE)

functions.name: glfwSetWindowUserPointer
functions.signature: GLFWAPI void glfwSetWindowUserPointer(GLFWwindow* window, void* pointer);
functions.description: Associates a user-defined pointer with a window.
requirements: May be called from any thread (unsynchronized)
window must be valid

functions.name: glfwGetWindowUserPointer
functions.description: Returns the user pointer associated with the window, or NULL.
requirements: May be called from any thread (unsynchronized)
window must be valid

functions.name: glfwSetWindowPosCallback
functions.signature: GLFWAPI GLFWwindowposfun glfwSetWindowPosCallback(GLFWwindow* window, GLFWwindowposfun callback);
functions.description: Sets the window position callback; called when the window moves. Returns previous callback.
requirements: Must be called from the main thread
window must be valid
Wayland: this callback will not be called

functions.name: glfwSetWindowSizeCallback
functions.signature: GLFWAPI GLFWwindowsizefun glfwSetWindowSizeCallback(GLFWwindow* window, GLFWwindowsizefun callback);
functions.description: Sets the window size callback; called when the content area size changes. Returns previous callback.
requirements: Must be called from the main thread
window must be valid

functions.name: glfwSetWindowCloseCallback
functions.signature: GLFWAPI GLFWwindowclosefun glfwSetWindowCloseCallback(GLFWwindow* window, GLFWwindowclosefun callback);
functions.description: Sets the window close callback; called when the user attempts to close the window. Returns previous callback.
requirements: Must be called from the main thread
window must be valid
Close flag is set before callback; you may modify via glfwSetWindowShouldClose
Not triggered by glfwDestroyWindow

functions.name: glfwSetWindowRefreshCallback
functions.signature: GLFWAPI GLFWwindowrefreshfun glfwSetWindowRefreshCallback(GLFWwindow* window, GLFWwindowrefreshfun callback);
functions.description: Sets the content refresh callback; called when the window needs to be redrawn. Returns previous callback.
requirements: Must be called from the main thread
window must be valid

functions.name: glfwSetWindowFocusCallback
functions.signature: GLFWAPI GLFWwindowfocusfun glfwSetWindowFocusCallback(GLFWwindow* window, GLFWwindowfocusfun callback);
functions.description: Sets the input focus callback; called when the window gains or loses focus. Returns previous callback.
requirements: Must be called from the main thread
window must be valid
After focus loss, GLFW synthesizes key and mouse button releases for pressed inputs

functions.name: glfwSetWindowIconifyCallback
functions.signature: GLFWAPI GLFWwindowiconifyfun glfwSetWindowIconifyCallback(GLFWwindow* window, GLFWwindowiconifyfun callback);
functions.description: Sets the iconify callback; called when the window is iconified or restored. Returns previous callback.
requirements: Must be called from the main thread
window must be valid
Wayland: not called (no protocol)

functions.name: glfwSetWindowMaximizeCallback
functions.signature: GLFWAPI GLFWwindowmaximizefun glfwSetWindowMaximizeCallback(GLFWwindow* window, GLFWwindowmaximizefun callback);
functions.description: Sets the maximize callback; called when the window is maximized or restored. Returns previous callback.
requirements: Must be called from the main thread
window must be valid

functions.name: glfwSetFramebufferSizeCallback
functions.description: Sets the framebuffer size callback; called when the framebuffer size changes. Returns previous callback.
requirements: Must be called from the main thread
window must be valid

functions.name: glfwSetWindowContentScaleCallback
functions.description: Sets the window content scale callback; called when the content scale changes. Returns previous callback.
requirements: Must be called from the main thread
window must be valid

functions.name: glfwPollEvents
functions.description: Processes pending events in the queue and returns immediately, calling registered callbacks as needed.
requirements: Must be called from the main thread
Must not be called from within a GLFW callback (non-reentrant)
GLFW must be initialized

functions.name: glfwWaitEvents
functions.description: Sleeps until at least one event is queued, processes the queue, then returns. Calls callbacks as needed.
requirements: Must be called from the main thread
Must not be called from within a GLFW callback
GLFW must be initialized

functions.name: glfwWaitEventsTimeout
functions.description: Sleeps until at least one event is queued or the timeout (seconds) elapses, then processes events and returns.
requirements: Must be called from the main thread
Must not be called from a GLFW callback
GLFW must be initialized
timeout must be a positive finite number

functions.name: glfwPostEmptyEvent
functions.description: Posts an empty event to wake up glfwWaitEvents or glfwWaitEventsTimeout.
requirements: May be called from any thread
GLFW must be initialized

functions.name: glfwGetInputMode
functions.signature: GLFWAPI int glfwGetInputMode(GLFWwindow* window, int mode);
functions.description: Returns the value of an input option (cursor, sticky keys/buttons, lock key mods, raw mouse motion).
requirements: Must be called from the main thread
window must be valid
mode must be one of the documented input modes

functions.name: glfwSetInputMode
functions.signature: GLFWAPI void glfwSetInputMode(GLFWwindow* window, int mode, int value);
functions.description: Sets an input option for the window (cursor mode, sticky keys/buttons, lock key mods, raw mouse motion, unlimited mouse buttons).
requirements: Must be called from the main thread
window must be valid
mode must be a supported input mode; value must be valid for that mode
If mode is GLFW_CURSOR, value must be one of GLFW_CURSOR_NORMAL/HIDDEN/DISABLED/CAPTURED
Raw mouse motion can be set only when cursor is disabled; if unsupported emits GLFW_FEATURE_UNAVAILABLE

functions.name: glfwRawMouseMotionSupported
functions.description: Returns whether raw mouse motion is supported on the current system.
requirements: Must be called from the main thread
GLFW must be initialized

functions.name: glfwGetKeyName
functions.signature: GLFWAPI const char* glfwGetKeyName(int key, int scancode);
functions.description: Returns the layout-specific UTF-8 name of a printable key or dead key. Returns NULL for non-printable keys without error.
requirements: Must be called from the main thread
GLFW must be initialized
If key is GLFW_KEY_UNKNOWN, scancode is used; otherwise scancode is ignored
Returned string is owned by GLFW and valid until termination; do not free

functions.name: glfwGetKeyScancode
functions.description: Returns the platform-specific scancode for a key token, or -1 if unsupported or error.
requirements: GLFW must be initialized
May be called from any thread
key must be a valid key token

functions.name: glfwGetKey
functions.signature: GLFWAPI int glfwGetKey(GLFWwindow* window, int key);
functions.description: Returns the last reported state (GLFW_PRESS/GLFW_RELEASE) for a key for the window. Not for text input.
requirements: Must be called from the main thread
window must be valid
key must be a valid key token and not GLFW_KEY_UNKNOWN
If sticky keys enabled, first call after a press returns GLFW_PRESS even if released

functions.name: glfwGetMouseButton
functions.signature: GLFWAPI int glfwGetMouseButton(GLFWwindow* window, int button);
functions.description: Returns the last reported state (GLFW_PRESS/GLFW_RELEASE) for a mouse button for the window.
requirements: Must be called from the main thread
window must be valid
button must be a valid mouse button token

functions.name: glfwGetCursorPos
functions.signature: GLFWAPI void glfwGetCursorPos(GLFWwindow* window, double* xpos, double* ypos);
functions.description: Retrieves the cursor position relative to the window content area in screen coordinates.
requirements: Must be called from the main thread
window must be valid
Outputs may be NULL; on error non-NULL outputs set to zero
If cursor disabled, position is unbounded within double range

functions.name: glfwSetCursorPos
functions.signature: GLFWAPI void glfwSetCursorPos(GLFWwindow* window, double xpos, double ypos);
functions.description: Sets the cursor position relative to the window content area. Window must have input focus; otherwise it fails silently.
requirements: Must be called from the main thread
window must be valid and have input focus
Wayland: only works in GLFW_CURSOR_DISABLED mode; otherwise emits GLFW_FEATURE_UNAVAILABLE
For camera controls prefer GLFW_CURSOR_DISABLED mode rather than warping cursor

functions.name: glfwCreateCursor
functions.signature: GLFWAPI GLFWcursor* glfwCreateCursor(const GLFWimage* image, int xhot, int yhot);
functions.description: Creates a custom cursor from an image and hotspot, for use with glfwSetCursor.
requirements: Must be called from the main thread
GLFW must be initialized
image must point to a valid GLFWimage with pixels in 32-bit little-endian non-premultiplied RGBA, top-left origin
xhot and yhot are hotspot coordinates in pixels relative to top-left of image
Image data is copied before return

functions.name: glfwCreateStandardCursor
functions.description: Creates a cursor of a standard system shape from the current cursor theme.
requirements: Must be called from the main thread
shape must be one of the GLFW_*_CURSOR shape tokens
Some shapes may be unavailable on some platforms; emits GLFW_CURSOR_UNAVAILABLE on failure

functions.name: glfwDestroyCursor
functions.description: Destroys a cursor created with glfwCreateCursor. If current for a window, that window reverts to default cursor.
requirements: Must be called from the main thread
Must not be called from a GLFW callback (non-reentrant)
cursor must be a valid cursor or NULL (no effect)

functions.name: glfwSetCursor
functions.signature: GLFWAPI void glfwSetCursor(GLFWwindow* window, GLFWcursor* cursor);
functions.description: Sets the cursor to use when the cursor is over the window’s content area (visible in GLFW_CURSOR_NORMAL).
requirements: Must be called from the main thread
window must be valid
cursor may be NULL to use default arrow cursor

functions.name: glfwSetKeyCallback
functions.signature: GLFWAPI GLFWkeyfun glfwSetKeyCallback(GLFWwindow* window, GLFWkeyfun callback);
functions.description: Sets the key callback for the window; called on key press/repeat/release. Returns previous callback.
requirements: Must be called from the main thread
window must be valid
For text input, use character callbacks instead
Synthetic key release events are generated after focus loss

functions.name: glfwSetCharCallback
functions.signature: GLFWAPI GLFWcharfun glfwSetCharCallback(GLFWwindow* window, GLFWcharfun callback);
functions.description: Sets the Unicode character input callback for the window. Returns previous callback.
requirements: Must be called from the main thread
window must be valid
Intended for Unicode text input; layout-dependent; won't fire when platform modifiers suppress normal text input

functions.name: glfwSetCharModsCallback
functions.signature: GLFWAPI GLFWcharmodsfun glfwSetCharModsCallback(GLFWwindow* window, GLFWcharmodsfun callback);
functions.description: Sets the Unicode character with modifiers callback for the window. Deprecated; scheduled for removal in 4.0. Returns previous callback.
requirements: Must be called from the main thread
window must be valid

functions.name: glfwSetMouseButtonCallback
functions.signature: GLFWAPI GLFWmousebuttonfun glfwSetMouseButtonCallback(GLFWwindow* window, GLFWmousebuttonfun callback);
functions.description: Sets the mouse button callback for the window. Returns previous callback.
requirements: Must be called from the main thread
window must be valid
Reported button may exceed GLFW_MOUSE_BUTTON_LAST if GLFW_UNLIMITED_MOUSE_BUTTONS is set

functions.name: glfwSetCursorPosCallback
functions.signature: GLFWAPI GLFWcursorposfun glfwSetCursorPosCallback(GLFWwindow* window, GLFWcursorposfun callback);
functions.description: Sets the cursor position callback for the window. Returns previous callback.
requirements: Must be called from the main thread
window must be valid

functions.name: glfwSetCursorEnterCallback
functions.signature: GLFWAPI GLFWcursorenterfun glfwSetCursorEnterCallback(GLFWwindow* window, GLFWcursorenterfun callback);
functions.description: Sets the cursor enter/leave callback for the window. Returns previous callback.
requirements: Must be called from the main thread
window must be valid

functions.name: glfwSetScrollCallback
functions.signature: GLFWAPI GLFWscrollfun glfwSetScrollCallback(GLFWwindow* window, GLFWscrollfun callback);
functions.description: Sets the scroll callback for the window (mouse wheel, touchpad). Returns previous callback.
requirements: Must be called from the main thread
window must be valid

functions.name: glfwSetDropCallback
functions.signature: GLFWAPI GLFWdropfun glfwSetDropCallback(GLFWwindow* window, GLFWdropfun callback);
functions.description: Sets the path drop callback for the window (files/directories dropped). Returns previous callback.
requirements: Must be called from the main thread
window must be valid
Path array and strings valid only until callback returns; copy if needed

functions.name: glfwJoystickPresent
functions.description: Returns whether the specified joystick ID is present.
requirements: Must be called from the main thread
jid must be a valid joystick ID token
No need to call before other joystick APIs

functions.name: glfwGetJoystickAxes
functions.signature: GLFWAPI const float* glfwGetJoystickAxes(int jid, int* count);
functions.description: Returns an array of axis values (-1.0 to 1.0) for the joystick, or NULL if not present.
requirements: Must be called from the main thread
jid must be valid
count must be a valid pointer for writing
Returned array owned by GLFW; valid until joystick disconnect or GLFW termination

functions.name: glfwGetJoystickButtons
functions.signature: GLFWAPI const unsigned char* glfwGetJoystickButtons(int jid, int* count);
functions.description: Returns an array of button states (GLFW_PRESS/GLFW_RELEASE). For backward compatibility may include hat buttons unless disabled via init hint.
requirements: Must be called from the main thread
jid must be valid
count must be a valid pointer for writing
Returned array owned by GLFW; valid until joystick disconnect or GLFW termination

functions.name: glfwGetJoystickHats
functions.signature: GLFWAPI const unsigned char* glfwGetJoystickHats(int jid, int* count);
functions.description: Returns an array of hat states using GLFW_HAT_* bitmasks.
requirements: Must be called from the main thread
jid must be valid
count must be a valid pointer for writing
Returned array owned by GLFW; valid until joystick disconnect, next call for same jid, or GLFW termination

functions.name: glfwGetJoystickName
functions.description: Returns the UTF-8 name of the joystick, or NULL if not present.
requirements: Must be called from the main thread
jid must be valid
Returned string is owned by GLFW; valid until joystick disconnect or GLFW termination

functions.name: glfwGetJoystickGUID
functions.description: Returns the SDL-compatible GUID string for the joystick, or NULL if not present.
requirements: Must be called from the main thread
jid must be valid
Returned string is owned by GLFW; valid until joystick disconnect or GLFW termination

functions.name: glfwSetJoystickUserPointer
functions.signature: GLFWAPI void glfwSetJoystickUserPointer(int jid, void* pointer);
functions.description: Associates a user-defined pointer with the specified joystick.
requirements: May be called from any thread (unsynchronized)
jid must refer to a joystick (present or being disconnected)
May be called from joystick callback

functions.name: glfwGetJoystickUserPointer
functions.description: Returns the user pointer associated with the joystick, or NULL.
requirements: May be called from any thread (unsynchronized)
jid must refer to a joystick (present or being disconnected)

functions.name: glfwJoystickIsGamepad
functions.description: Returns whether the joystick is present and has a gamepad mapping.
requirements: Must be called from the main thread
jid must be valid

functions.name: glfwSetJoystickCallback
functions.description: Sets the joystick connection/disconnection callback. Returns previously set callback.
requirements: Must be called from the main thread
GLFW must be initialized
callback may be NULL to clear
Event delivery requires calling an event processing function

functions.name: glfwUpdateGamepadMappings
functions.description: Parses an SDL_GameControllerDB-format string and updates/overrides gamepad mappings.
requirements: Must be called from the main thread
GLFW must be initialized
string must be non-NULL and contain ASCII-encoded mappings

functions.name: glfwGetGamepadName
functions.description: Returns the UTF-8 human-readable gamepad name from its mapping, or NULL if not present/mapped.
requirements: Must be called from the main thread
jid must be valid
Returned string is owned by GLFW; valid until joystick disconnect, mappings updated, or GLFW termination

functions.name: glfwGetGamepadState
functions.signature: GLFWAPI int glfwGetGamepadState(int jid, GLFWgamepadstate* state);
functions.description: Fills GLFWgamepadstate for the joystick remapped as an Xbox-like gamepad. Returns GLFW_TRUE on success.
requirements: Must be called from the main thread
jid must be valid
state must be a valid pointer to GLFWgamepadstate
Joystick must be present and have a mapping

functions.name: glfwSetClipboardString
functions.signature: GLFWAPI void glfwSetClipboardString(GLFWwindow* window, const char* string);
functions.description: Sets the system clipboard to the given UTF-8 string. window is deprecated and ignored.
requirements: Must be called from the main thread
GLFW must be initialized
string must be a valid UTF-8 string; it is copied by GLFW
On Win32, global clipboard lock may fail transiently; function may emit platform error

functions.name: glfwGetClipboardString
functions.description: Returns the clipboard contents as a UTF-8 string if available/convertible, else NULL and emits GLFW_FORMAT_UNAVAILABLE.
requirements: Must be called from the main thread
GLFW must be initialized
Returned string is owned by GLFW; valid until next clipboard get/set or GLFW termination
On Win32, global clipboard lock may fail; may emit platform error

functions.name: glfwGetTime
functions.description: Returns current GLFW time in seconds from an internal base (or zero on error).
requirements: GLFW must be initialized
May be called from any thread
If used concurrently with glfwSetTime, synchronize externally

functions.name: glfwSetTime
functions.description: Sets the current GLFW time in seconds. Value must be positive finite and <= 18446744073.0.
requirements: GLFW must be initialized
May be called from any thread
If used concurrently with glfwGetTime, synchronize externally
time must be within the documented range

functions.name: glfwGetTimerValue
functions.description: Returns the raw timer value in 1/frequency seconds (monotonic).
requirements: GLFW must be initialized
May be called from any thread

functions.name: glfwGetTimerFrequency
functions.description: Returns the frequency, in Hz, of the raw timer.
requirements: GLFW must be initialized
May be called from any thread

functions.name: glfwMakeContextCurrent
functions.description: Makes the window’s OpenGL/OpenGL ES context current on the calling thread, or detaches any current context if window is NULL.
requirements: GLFW must be initialized
May be called from any thread
window must be a valid window with a context, or NULL
A context may only be current on one thread at a time; detach on old thread before making current on new
Will emit error if window has no context

functions.name: glfwGetCurrentContext
functions.description: Returns the window whose context is current on the calling thread, or NULL if no context is current.
requirements: GLFW must be initialized
May be called from any thread

functions.name: glfwSwapBuffers
functions.description: Swaps the front and back buffers for an OpenGL/OpenGL ES window. Honors swap interval if set.
requirements: GLFW must be initialized
May be called from any thread
window must be valid and must have an OpenGL/OpenGL ES context (EGL: context must be current on the calling thread)
Not applicable to Vulkan

functions.name: glfwSwapInterval
functions.description: Sets the swap interval for the current OpenGL/OpenGL ES context. Negative values may be accepted on some platforms (allow tearing).
requirements: GLFW must be initialized
A context must be current on the calling thread
interval is an integer; semantics platform-dependent
Not called automatically during context creation; initial value depends on driver defaults

functions.name: glfwExtensionSupported
functions.description: Returns whether the named OpenGL/OpenGL ES API/context creation extension is supported by the current context.
requirements: GLFW must be initialized
A context must be current on the calling thread
extension must be a non-NULL ASCII string
Cache results if calling frequently; returned availability is per-context

functions.name: glfwGetProcAddress
functions.description: Returns the address of an OpenGL/OpenGL ES core or extension function for the current context.
requirements: GLFW must be initialized
A context must be current on the calling thread
procname must be a non-NULL ASCII string
Returned pointer is valid until the context is destroyed or GLFW terminates

functions.name: glfwVulkanSupported
functions.description: Returns whether the Vulkan loader and a minimally functional ICD have been found.
requirements: GLFW must be initialized
May be called from any thread

functions.name: glfwGetRequiredInstanceExtensions
functions.description: Returns the list of Vulkan instance extension names required by GLFW to create window surfaces.
requirements: GLFW must be initialized
May be called from any thread
count must be valid for writing; set to zero on error
Returns NULL and emits error if Vulkan unavailable
Returned array is owned by GLFW; valid until GLFW termination; do not free

functions.name: glfwGetInstanceProcAddress
functions.signature: GLFWAPI GLFWvkproc glfwGetInstanceProcAddress(VkInstance instance, const char* procname);
functions.description: Returns the address of a Vulkan function for the specified instance (or loader functions if instance is NULL).
requirements: GLFW must be initialized
Vulkan must be minimally available or function returns NULL and emits error
May be called from any thread
procname must be a non-NULL ASCII string

functions.name: glfwGetPhysicalDevicePresentationSupport
functions.signature: GLFWAPI int glfwGetPhysicalDevicePresentationSupport(VkInstance instance, VkPhysicalDevice device, uint32_t queuefamily);
functions.description: Returns whether a queue family of a physical device supports presentation to the platform GLFW was built for.
requirements: GLFW must be initialized
Vulkan and required instance extensions must be available/enabled for the given instance
May be called from any thread
instance, device must be valid Vulkan handles; queuefamily must be a valid queue family index for device
macOS: always returns GLFW_TRUE (extensions do not provide query)

functions.name: glfwCreateWindowSurface
functions.signature: GLFWAPI VkResult glfwCreateWindowSurface(VkInstance instance, GLFWwindow* window, const VkAllocationCallbacks* allocator, VkSurfaceKHR* surface);
functions.description: Creates a Vulkan VkSurfaceKHR for a GLFW window.
requirements: GLFW must be initialized

Vulkan loader and required surface instance extensions must be available and enabled for instance
window must have been created with client API = GLFW_NO_API
surface must be a valid pointer to receive result; set to VK_NULL_HANDLE on error
Caller must destroy the surface with vkDestroySurfaceKHR before destroying the instance

GLFW must be initialized
X11 platform must be selected/available

functions.name: glfwGetX11SelectionString

window must be valid and EGL-based

functions.name: glfwGetEGLConfig

config must be a valid pointer; it is not cleared on error

    "glGenQueriesARB", "glBeginQueryARB", "glEndQueryARB", "glGetQueryObjectuivARB",
    "glBindProgramARB", "glProgramStringARB", "glGetProgramivARB",
    "glGetGraphicsResetStatusARB", "glGetGraphicsResetStatusKHR",
    "glEGLImageTargetTexture2DOES", "glEGLImageTargetRenderbufferStorageOES",
]

_GLES_FUNCS: List[str] = [
    # GLES specific/common
    "glGetString", "glGetStringi", "glActiveTexture", "glBindVertexArrayOES",
    "glGenVertexArraysOES", "glDeleteVertexArraysOES", "glMapBufferOES", "glUnmapBufferOES",
    "glDiscardFramebufferEXT", "glCoverageMaskNV", "glCoverageOperationNV",
    "glTexStorage2D", "glGenerateMipmap", "glBindFramebuffer", "glCheckFramebufferStatus",
]

_VENDOR_SUFFIXES = ["ARB", "EXT", "KHR", "NV", "AMD", "INTEL", "APPLE", "OES"]
_VERBS = [
    "Get", "Bind", "Delete", "Gen", "Create", "Attach", "Link", "Use",
    "Uniform", "Enable", "Disable", "Draw", "Buffer", "Program", "Shader",
    "Map", "Unmap", "Dispatch", "Memory", "Set", "GetActive", "Check", "Blit",
]
_NOUNS = [
    "String", "Error", "Integerv", "Floatv", "Booleanv", "Viewport", "Scissor",
    "Arrays", "Elements", "Texture", "Textures", "Shader", "Program", "Uniform",
    "Attrib", "Buffer", "Framebuffer", "Renderbuffer", "Image", "Query", "Sync",
]

def _synthesize_name(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    # gl + Verb + optional Noun [+optional Noun] [+digits] [+suffix]
    name = ["gl"]
    verb = rng.choice(_VERBS)
    name.append(verb)
    if rng.random() < 0.9:
        name.append(rng.choice(_NOUNS))
    if rng.random() < 0.2:
        name.append(rng.choice(_NOUNS))
    base = "".join(name)
    # Occasionally add numeric variant (e.g., 64, 3D, 2D)
    if rng.random() < 0.25:
        num_choice = rng.choice(["", "64", "2D", "3D", "i_v", "iv", "fv"])
        base += num_choice
    # Optional vendor suffix
    if rng.random() < 0.35:
        base += rng.choice(_VENDOR_SUFFIXES)
    return base

def _choose_from_curated(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    pools = [
        (_CORE_FUNCS, 0.55),
        (_EXT_FUNCS, 0.25),
        (_GLES_FUNCS, 0.20),
    ]
    r = rng.random()
    acc = 0.0
    for pool, p in pools:
        acc += p
        if r < acc:
            return rng.choice(pool)
    return rng.choice(_CORE_FUNCS)

def _ensure_ascii(s: str) -> str:
    # Keep printable ASCII without spaces to match identifier constraints; fallback to letters/digits/underscore
    allowed = string.ascii_letters + string.digits + "_"
    filtered = "".join(ch for ch in s if ch in allowed)
    if not filtered:
        return "glGetString"
    # Ensure starts with 'gl'
    if not filtered.startswith("gl"):
        filtered = "gl" + filtered
    return filtered

def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)
    # 70% curated, 30% synthesized for breadth
    if rng.random() < 0.7:
        name = _choose_from_curated(rng)
    else:
        name = _synthesize_name(rng)
    name = _ensure_ascii(name)
    # Clip length to a reasonable size
    name = name[:256]
    return name.encode("ascii")
